newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Supreme Court denies unfair treatment of Megawati.
newsitem.headline: Supreme Court denies unfair treatment of Megawati.

text.p: Indonesia's Supreme Court has denied allegations that judges had been swayed by government pressure in cases involving ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, the Merdeka newspaper said on Wednesday.

The newspaper quoted Chief Justice Sarwata (Eds: one word) as denying on Tuesday that the Supreme Court, which oversees all the nation's courts, had been pressed by the government to overturn all the suits filed by Megawati regarding her ouster.
"There is no such thing. We keep abiding by the law and the Constitution," Sarwata said without elaborating.
A Supreme Court spokesman confirmed the report, but declined to comment further.

Eighty lawyers backing Megawati submitted a petition to the Supreme Court last month demanding an explanation about reports that government officials had requested courts to prepare ways of dismissing all Megawati lawsuits on technical grounds.

Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, has sued the government and the military over her government-backed dismissal last June from the leadership of the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

The Central Jakarta district court, which heard a case against the armed forces chief, interior minister, and Megawati's political rivals, dismissed the suit last year, saying it did not have the authority to rule on an internal party matter.
Megawati appealed the verdict and the case is now before the High Court, one step below the Supreme Court.

Merdeka quoted Sarwata as saying the secretary-general of the Supreme Court had received the lawyers' petition and had said that people who were not satisfied with decisions made by lower courts could always file an appeal. It gave no further details.
Megawati's supporters have filed about 130 suits against her removal in courts across Indonesia, and many cases have been rejected on technical grounds. They have not yet won a case.
The minority PDI, the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and the ruling Golkar are the only political parties legally permitted to contest the general elections on May 29.
